sources.title: Annual report / financial results
sources.supports: latest financial anchor used in packet

financial_anchor.caveat: FY2025 profit from recurring operations governs the pre-tax recurring-profit screen.

ai_claim.claim: LVMH describes scoped AI/digital mechanisms in localized demand/allocation and clienteling analytics, generative assistance for marketing and internal knowledge.
ai_claim.stage: E1; E2 only where management explicitly reports production use
ai_claim.scope: full-price sell-through, inventory turns, repeat purchase at fixed cohort, conversion and contribution after creative/model cost
ai_claim.limitation: No controlled quality-adjusted company result tied to retained incremental cash was found.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Kering and digital-native premium brands and general commerce/creative platforms can replicate tools or force gains through to customers.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Competitive capability does not by itself prove equal outcomes.

rights_limit: Client data, imagery, artist and talent rights are purpose- and maison-specific. Public policy does not show broad cross-maison training permission.
materiality_summary: Five percent of the completed-year governing metric is €890m; public evidence does not establish an AI-attributed amount.

arithmetic.inputs: FY2025 profit from recurring operations €17.8bn; 5%; illustrative eligible pool €5bn, efficiency 8%, realization 50%, retention 50%, recurring cost €80m
arithmetic.result: Illustrative €20m is below the €890m annual pre-tax recurring-profit hurdle; no AI-attributed amount is established.

g2_provisional: Open: E1/E2 evidence supports measurement, but E3 quality-adjusted causality and E4 cash retention are not established.
unresolved_questions: What share of eligible workload is in production?
What controlled quality-adjusted KPI result exists?
What do contracts permit for pooled learning and how much benefit is retained after recurring cost?
